header.note: Every string the terminal administration shows, and the page of the loopback interface the browser is answered with once it brought the authorization response back. ICU message format: {issuer} is the issuer of the tenant, {profile} the name the profile of the instance was kept under, {administrator} the name of who signed in, {acr} the class of their authentication, {url} the address of the authorization endpoint, {redirect_uri} the redirect URI of the client, {reason} why the sign-in or a read of the administration API failed, {minutes} and {time} how long the access token is worth and until when, {time} also when a session was authenticated, {days} a number of days, {count} a number of rows, {client} the identifier of a client, {username} the username the administrator typed or the API answered, {kind} and {name} the kind and the name of a credential, {address} the address a session was last seen from, {since} the start of the window the statistics count over. value.more is a printf pattern, %d being how many items were left out. A string named refusal.<error> is what the screen says to do when the provider refuses a sign-in with that error, api.refusal.<error> when the administration API refuses a request with it, act.<name> how the screen names an act of the journal, and key.status.<state> how it names the state of a signing key.

trans-unit.target: Enter opens the sign-in of the instance in the browser. An administrator signs in with a passkey.

Copy this value now for whoever registers the client: it will not be shown again. Enter closes it. Logged under your name.

Type a username, then Enter. Every read of a person is logged under your name.

Enter on a group shows its members. Every read of a member is logged under your name.
Nobody is a member of this group.

Group {group} created. Logged under your name.
{username} is a member of {group}. Logged under your name.
Take {username} out of {group}? y confirms, any other key cancels.
Take {username} out of {group}? It is their last administering group: they will no longer administer the tenant. y confirms, any other key cancels.
{username} is no longer a member of {group}. Logged under your name.
Revoke the {kind} credential {name} of {username}? It can no longer be used. y confirms, any other key cancels.

Enable {username} again? Their old sessions do not come back. y confirms, any other key cancels.

Account of {username} enabled again. Logged under your name.

A password is replaced, never revoked, and a revoked credential stays revoked.
End the session of {username} authenticated {time} from {address}? Its applications are told. y confirms, any other key cancels.
Session of {username} ended, its applications told. Logged under your name.
Revoke the consent {username} gave {application}? What it was issued is revoked, except an access token already issued, valid until it expires. y confirms, any other key cancels.
Consent {username} gave {application} revoked. Logged under your name.
sign-ins to a SAML service provider
changes of the contact of the tenant
You can close this window and go back to the terminal.
An administrator signs in with a passkey, never with a password alone. Add one on the passkeys page of your account.
This account does not administer the instance: it must be a member of a group named in BEFFROI_TENANT_ADMINISTRATORS. If you refused the consent, start again and accept it.
This client cannot ask for the administration API: register this machine again with the identifier in BEFFROI_TENANT_ADMINISTRATION_RESOURCE.
Account {username} created, with no credential: t issues a link to add a passkey. Logged under your name.
Issue a link to add a passkey for {username}? Whoever holds it can add one until it expires. The previous link stops working. y confirms, any other key cancels.
{link} is valid until {time}. Scan the code with the device that will hold the passkey; the link disappears when the focus moves. Logged under your name.
The terminal is too small for the code: it needs {columns} columns and {rows} lines.
Issue a new password link for {username}? Whoever holds it can set one until it expires, which ends all their sessions. The previous link stops working. y confirms, any other key cancels.
{link} is valid until {time}. Scan the code with the device where the person will type their password; the link disappears when the focus moves. Logged under your name.

Issue a new authenticator app link for {username}? Whoever holds it can set one up until it expires, which revokes the old one and ends all their sessions. The previous link stops working. y confirms, any other key cancels.
{link} is valid until {time}. Scan the code with the device where the person will set up their app; the link disappears when the focus moves. Logged under your name.
